as_told.title: Bill Gunston: Brown's work went into the B-2

plain: The story is that an aviation writer named Bill Gunston published an article arguing that the B-2 stealth bomber could not fly as well as it does by ordinary means. The suggestion is that it gets an extra push from electrogravitics, a claimed way of moving aircraft with powerful electric fields. The aviation journalist Nick Cook tells Michels about "this astounding article": when you work through the B-2's weight and engines, it "would have been incapable of the performance figures credited for it." Cook credits it to Air International magazine. In another telling Cook says only that the performance data "does not add up" and does not mention electrogravitics. Michels gives it a sharper edge. He says Gunston was "very sure" that the work of the researcher Townsend Brown on electric propulsion "made it in the B2", and he dates the article to 2000, where the story places it in the 1990s. If true, it would mean anti-gravity-style technology is already flying in an American bomber.
